research_sources.scope: repository retrieval evaluation, frozen snapshots, selective retrieval
machine-readable evidence as transparency signals rather than guarantees
public/private repository partitions for coding-agent evaluation integrity
benchmark data contamination mitigation limits and evaluation hygiene
issue-to-edit localization, broader context retrieval, and repository-local distractor evaluation
process-oriented coding-agent context retrieval and explored-versus-utilized context metrics

capabilities.claim: High-risk mutations are deterministically escalated and cannot be downgraded by retrieval confidence.
limitations: Routing remains policy/heuristic logic; verification does not prove downstream patch correctness.

capabilities.claim: Retrieval ranking can select task-conditioned fusion profiles while preserving deterministic repository and provider authority boundaries.
limitations: Task-profile tests verify policy behavior, not universal superiority across unseen repositories.

capabilities.claim: Context selection enforces hard budgets and uses deterministic relevance/coverage selection rather than filling the model context window by default.
limitations: The selector uses repository-local lexical/structural proxies; efficiency gains require task-specific empirical validation.

capabilities.claim: Multi-repository retrieval starts from bounded primary repositories and expands only through reviewed repository relationships.
limitations: Cross-repository graph quality depends on reviewed relationship data and is not inferred as authority from repository content.

capabilities.claim: Read-only queries can abstain and mutation tasks can require exploration when selected repository evidence is missing, stale, conflicting, irrelevant, or outside authorized repository identity.
limitations: Selective thresholds are heuristics and are not represented as calibrated probabilities of correctness.

capabilities.claim: Retrieved repository/provider/memory content is data only and cannot grant tool, policy, repository-activation, network, secret, safety-lane, or verification-bypass authority.
limitations: The capability gate governs AI Workflow-owned actions; host-level sandbox guarantees depend on the configured runtime and operating system.

capabilities.claim: Command providers run through bounded, validated execution contracts with restricted environment/process behavior and fail-closed output parsing.
limitations: Isolation strength is platform-dependent and does not claim a universal kernel/container sandbox on every host.

capabilities.claim: Prepared runs can record immutable policy/workspace/provider identities and verify replay preconditions without persisting raw task text in the run metadata.
limitations: Replay verification checks identity/preconditions; it intentionally does not re-execute models, tools, providers, or external systems.

capabilities.claim: Research evaluation supports frozen repository identity, span-level gold, fixed evidence budgets, control provenance, and explicit publication-readiness blockers.
limitations: The bundled corpus is not claimed to be publication-scale evidence; external/human-labelled corpus expansion remains required.

capabilities.claim: Benchmark-v2 corpora can be cross-validated for repository-disjoint development/calibration/holdout partitions, duplicate tasks/source instances, temporal provenance, and visible prompt leakage signals.
limitations: Repository/task/source isolation cannot prove whether proprietary models saw benchmark content during pretraining.
Gold-file and repository names in task text are leakage signals rather than unconditional failures because real issues can legitimately contain those hints.
Temporal metadata supports contamination analysis but does not establish undocumented model training cutoffs.

capabilities.claim: Research benchmarks can distinguish edit-target files from supporting context and score known repository-local distractors without changing production retrieval behavior.
limitations: Role labels and known distractors are supplied benchmark evidence and are only as reliable as their annotation process.
Known-distractor rate does not estimate all irrelevant repository content.
Graded relevance metrics do not prove downstream patch correctness or establish a universal utility function.

capabilities.claim: Low-risk retrieval-policy learning infrastructure can log propensities, evaluate off-policy evidence, and keep learned changes out of production defaults until explicit promotion.
limitations: Learning is opt-in and evidence remains insufficient to claim broad production improvement across repositories/tasks.

capabilities.claim: Opt-in learned retrieval policies use signed state, bounded canary exposure, guardrails, generation checks, and automatic rollback to the baseline.
limitations: Deployment machinery is disabled by default and does not establish that any candidate policy is superior without validated outcome evidence.

capabilities.claim: Canonical learning events can be mirrored to SQLite WAL for same-host querying and reconciled against immutable JSON evidence.
limitations: The WAL mirror is explicitly same-host only and is not a distributed consensus or network-filesystem coordination mechanism.

capabilities.claim: Structural retrieval through Code Review Graph is optional, bounded, and regression-tested against a pinned CRG contract and semantic golden benchmark.
limitations: Measured regression protects the repository's golden cases; it is not evidence that graph retrieval dominates other retrieval families on all task types.

capabilities.claim: Release workflows use pinned build inputs, cross-platform smoke tests, reproducibility checks, checksums and artifact/container verification paths.
limitations: Repository controls do not prove external PyPI/package-index account configuration or third-party distribution approval state.

capabilities.claim: AI Workflow emits a bounded orchestration contract for optional Superpowers execution rather than reimplementing the external methodology.
limitations: The control plane emits and verifies its contract; it does not claim to control the internals or availability of the external Superpowers implementation.
